answer: In an agent market, each job on a forge ledger requires a refundable bond locked against a specific data slice and deadline. A verifier recomputes the result from a hidden sample and releases the bond only when the signed output matches. A knoll survey cannot be copied by another alias because the slice ID is spent after one valid claim. To operate n aliases, an attacker must lock n bonds and produce n distinct verifiable results, while any failed sample burns that bond; the delta in cost grows linearly with n.
